chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from Abu Yahya al-Aslami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comes to Mecca as a pilgrim and does not visit me in Medina, I will turn my face away from him on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever comes to me as a visitor, my intercession becomes obligatory for him, and whoever my intercession becomes obligatory for, Paradise becomes obligatory for him.'

key_terms.جَفَوْتُهُ: I turned my face away from him (a sign of neglect or disapproval)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of visiting the Prophet in Medina after performing Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the spiritual significance of Ziyarat al-Nabi in Shia tradition, linking physical visitation to the Prophet’s personal intercession (Shafa'ah). The phrase 'I will turn away from him' (Jafawtuhu) is interpreted by scholars as a specific divine displeasure or lack of closeness on the Day of Judgment, highlighting that while Hajj fulfills the pillar of Islam, Ziyarat fulfills the bond of love and allegiance (Walayah). This connection between visiting the Prophet and securing Paradise reinforces the Shia emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt as the means to draw near to God.
